methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting the technology gap in Hampton Roads signal grassroots capability-building outside traditional tech hubs, demonstrating distributed peer-learning infrastructure that could counter metro concentration.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for deep AI education and community impact in Richmond, establishing a secondary hub that could distribute capability beyond NoVA's dominance.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents deliberate capability-building in a non-metro region, creating potential for distributed deep learning networks if it scales beyond institutional boundaries into broader community adoption.

signals.title: Virginia Tech secures $20m NSF grant for AI-enabled semiconductor lab - Cleanroom Technology
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's $20M NSF grant for AI-enabled semiconductor research concentrates cutting-edge technical capability in Blacksburg, but without explicit workforce distribution mechanisms risks reinforcing the excellence-in-isolation pattern.

signals.title: After severe 76% electricity price hikes due to AI data centers, Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure — state regulators crack down, governor says move will save civilians ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’ - tomshardware.com
signals.signal_reading: The 76% electricity price hike from NoVA data centers imposing costs on civilians statewide reveals how concentrated AI infrastructure can create economic burdens that widen gaps rather than distribute benefits, potentially undermining public support for broader AI adoption.
